Subject: Dedicated reservation: sizing and ramp options for UmbraGen

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We walked the platform with product and infra today and we have a clearer picture of the traffic profile: heavy embeddings at scale (2M queries/day projected by Jan) plus short bursts of high‑quality generation for our assistant features.

Two asks as we prep our budget and procurement timeline:
- Can you outline 2–3 recommended dedicated reservation options (cluster size / min GPUs) that balance unit cost and headroom for bursts?
- We need a practical ramp schedule tied to our Q4 pilot and full production in Q1. Prefer a plan that minimizes upfront commit but gives predictable throughput.

I attached a short traffic forecast and product notes (see umbragen_capacity_model_v2.xlsx). We also have a compliance checkpoint in mid‑October — if there are specific logs/controls tied to a private deployment, flag those too.

Goal: get a short options document and a ballpark price so we can take to procurement next week.

Appreciate it —
Eleanor

Eleanor —

Thanks for the forecast and the context. I looped in Monica (onboarding/ops) and Ben (commercial) so we can align on both technical sizing and commercial structure. High level, here are three pragmatic options we recommend based on the profile you shared:

Option A — Lean baseline (lower commit, higher burst reliance)
- Minimum committed cluster: 8 x H100 (baseline lane)
- Burst capacity: up to 24 GPUs via burst pool (subject to availability windows)
- Ramp schedule: 8 GPUs at contract start, automatic +4 GPUs at month 3, review/commit at month 6
- Use case fit: pilot with predictable daytime load + intermittent spikes
- Notes: higher unit cost for burst; warm prefix caching recommended to control latency for embeddings

Option B — Balanced throughput (recommended mid path)
- Minimum committed cluster: 16 x H100
- Burst capacity: up to 40 GPUs with priority burst lanes and reserved warmup buffer
- Ramp schedule: 8 GPUs active month 0 (can be prewarmed for canary), scale to 16 by month 2, then +8 optional at month 5 if 30‑day throughput > 25% above forecast
- Use case fit: production pilot with sustained embeddings traffic and some generative peaks
- Notes: better unit economics, recommend prefix KV caching and batching for embeddings to cut cost ~30%

Option C — Anchored capacity (predictable performance, lower risk)
- Minimum committed cluster: 32 x H100
- Burst capacity: dedicated surge lanes up to 64 GPUs (SLA-backed during business hours)
- Ramp schedule: 16 GPUs month 0, 32 GPUs month 1 (transitional credits available)
- Use case fit: full production with strict latency/throughput SLOs
- Notes: lowest effective per‑token cost and strongest SLA placement; best for teams forecasting >5M queries/day

Commercial framing and elasticity
- We can tie a 12‑month reserved contract to either a staircase ramp (credits for early months) or a smoothing plan where you pay a steady monthly commit with a seasonal true‑up.
- We also offer an automatic fallback to our hosted-compatible model variants (smaller model or quantized profile) if capacity is constrained — useful for handling unexpected peak loads without degrading end user experience.

Next steps
1) Monica will run a quick capacity simulation against the file you attached and share a slots/day view.
2) Ben will produce a ballpark pricing snapshot for Option A/B/C (ballpark by EOD tomorrow).
3) If you agree, we'll prepare a 1‑page options PDF and a short canary run plan you can hand to procurement.

I've attached a draft we typically share for deals like this (UG_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf).

Best —
Markus

Carlos —

Answers below; copying Monica and Ben for follow up items.

1) Pro‑rata & commit rhythm
- The optional +8 at month 5 can be structured either as a calendar pro‑rata (monthly true‑up where the additional GPUs bill pro‑rata from activation date) or as a step commitment that resets the baseline for the remainder of the term.
- If procurement prefers smoothing, we recommend the steady‑pay model with a 6‑month true‑up that reconciles actual usage to committed units. Ben — we should include a sample 12‑month cashflow showing both approaches for UmbraGen.

2) Audit/SLA & burst lanes
- Audit logs and request tracing: available for Dedicated and Private deployments. Monica will prepare the exact log retention and schema (we support request IDs, token‑level latency traces, and KV cache hit metrics).
- SLA: burst lanes are offered with a priority tier — if you purchase a business‑hours surge SLA (Option C style), we can commit to surge availability and include a credits schedule. For Option B, burst is best‑effort unless you add the surge SLA add‑on.

Action items:
- Monica will share the capacity simulation + retention/logs doc by Monday.
- Ben will attach the two commercial framing examples (step commit vs smoothing) and a sample monthly cashflow.
- I'll prep the 1‑pager and the short canary plan for procurement to review (DocuSign link will follow).

We can also run a 2‑week canary (8 GPU baseline) that demonstrates latency and cost curves before procurement signs — helpful for the compliance team.

Thanks —
Markus
